definition_zh: 互动的；交互式的；相互作用的；（设备或软件）可双向操作的
definition_en: acting on or responding to one another; involving two-way communication between people, or between a user and a machine that reacts to input
core_image: 手指点向屏幕，屏幕随即亮起并改变画面：一方动作，另一方马上回应
scene: 博物馆里，孩子伸手触碰展项屏幕，讲解员说这是交互式展项。This exhibit is interactive, so the picture changes when you touch the screen.

senses.title: Mutually acting
senses.definition: describing two or more things that act on each other and produce effects on both sides
senses.definitionCN: 描述两个或更多事物彼此施力、双方都受影响
senses.example: The study models interactive forces inside the cell.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究对细胞内部相互作用的力进行建模。
senses.why: Interactive is interaction turned into an adjective: inter- 'between' + act, from Latin agere 'to do'. The -ive suffix makes it a property, so the word says that a relationship has two active ends rather than one.
senses.whyCN: interactive 是 interaction 转成的形容词：inter-“在……之间”+ act，源自拉丁语 agere“做”。-ive 后缀把它变成一种属性，因此这个词表示一种关系有两个活动的端点，而不是一个。

senses.title: Involving people in exchange
senses.definition: describing communication in which people speak, listen, and respond to one another
senses.definitionCN: 描述人们彼此说、听、回应的交流
senses.example: The workshop was interactive, with every participant speaking twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这场工作坊是互动式的，每位参与者都发言了两次。
senses.why: Applied to people, the adjective describes a pattern rather than a device: turns alternate, and each turn depends on the last. It contrasts with 'lecture-style', where information flows one way.
senses.whyCN: 用在人身上时，这个形容词描述一种模式而非设备：轮次交替，每一轮都取决于上一轮。它与“讲座式”相对，后者信息只朝一个方向流。

senses.title: Responding to user input
senses.titleCN: （设备）对用户操作作出回应的
senses.definition: describing a device, screen, or program that reacts immediately to what a user does
senses.definitionCN: 描述对用户操作立即作出反应的设备、屏幕或程序
senses.example: The new kiosk is fully interactive and works without a keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 新的自助终端完全交互式，无需键盘即可使用。
senses.why: This is the computing sense recorded in the 1960s: a program is interactive when it waits for input and answers it. The machine is cast as a partner in the loop, not as a one-way display.
senses.whyCN: 这是 1960 年代记录的计算机义：程序等待输入并回应输入，就是交互式的。机器被设定为回路中的伙伴，而不是单向的显示器。

senses.title: Open to audience participation
senses.definition: describing an exhibition, performance, or broadcast that invites the audience to take part
senses.definitionCN: 描述邀请观众参与其中的展览、演出或节目
senses.example: The gallery's interactive installation lets visitors draw on the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆的互动装置让观众可以在墙上作画。
senses.why: Museums and media borrowed the computing sense and shifted the partner from a machine to an audience. What stays constant is the invitation: the work is unfinished until someone acts.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与媒体借用了计算机义，把伙伴从机器换成了观众。不变的是那份邀请：作品在有人行动之前尚未完成。

senses.title: Two-way in teaching
senses.definition: describing teaching in which students ask, answer, and act rather than only listen
senses.definitionCN: 描述学生提问、回答、行动而不只是听讲的教学
senses.example: Interactive teaching raised the number of questions students asked.
senses.exampleCN: 互动教学提高了学生提问的数量。
senses.why: Education reform used the adjective as a slogan against passive instruction. The word measures the number of directions in which information travels, so a lecture with questions counts as interactive.
senses.whyCN: 教育改革把这个形容词当作反对被动灌输的口号。这个词衡量信息传播的方向数，所以带提问的讲授也算 interactive。

senses.title: Interactive mode in computing
senses.definition: describing a program or session that accepts commands and returns results immediately instead of running a fixed batch
senses.definitionCN: 描述立即接受命令并返回结果、而非按固定批处理运行的程序或会话
senses.example: Switch to interactive mode to test each query as you type it.
senses.exampleCN: 切换到交互模式，就可以边输入边测试每条查询。
senses.why: In computing, 'interactive' contrasts with 'batch': a batch job runs alone, while an interactive one waits and answers. The technical difference is where the human sits inside the loop.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域里 interactive 与 batch（批处理）相对：批处理任务独自运行，交互式任务则等待并回答。技术差别就在于人坐在回路的哪个位置。

senses.title: Mutually influencing in a process
senses.definition: describing a process or relationship in which each change produces a further change in the other party
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种过程或关系，其中一方的变化又引起另一方变化
senses.example: The report describes an interactive cycle of warming and melting.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了一个变暖与融化的相互影响循环。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes feedback rather than interface: warming melts ice, melting darkens the surface, darkening speeds warming. The word names the circle, not any single step.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词描述反馈而非界面：变暖融冰，融冰使地表变暗，变暗又加速变暖。这个词命名的是圆圈，而不是任何单一步骤。

senses.title: Playable in games and media
senses.definition: describing entertainment in which the player's choices change what happens next
senses.definitionCN: 描述玩家的选择会改变后续情节的娱乐形式
senses.example: The novel became an interactive story in which readers choose the ending.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说变成了互动故事，读者可以选择结局。
senses.why: Games and digital fiction extend the computing sense to narrative: the work branches according to input. 'Interactive' here means that the audience has authority over the outcome, however small.
senses.whyCN: 游戏与数字小说把计算机义扩展到叙事：作品随输入分岔。这里的 interactive 意味着观众对结局拥有决定权，无论这权力多小。

intro.en: Interactive is the adjective of interact, itself a back-formation from interaction. The parts are still visible: inter- 'between' plus act, from Latin agere 'to do'. Its computing sense is a twentieth-century specialization of a nineteenth-century word.
intro.cn: interactive 是 interact 的形容词，而 interact 又是 interaction 的逆构词。成分仍清晰可见：inter-“在……之间”加 act，源自拉丁语 agere“做”。它的计算机义是 19 世纪旧词在 20 世纪的专业化延伸。

items.en: Latin agere 'to do, drive' supplied actus and actio. The preposition inter 'between' could combine with almost any verb, giving the pattern 'do something between two parties'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 agere“做、驱动”提供了 actus 与 actio。介词 inter“在……之间”几乎能与任何动词组合，形成“在两方之间做某事”的模式。

items.en: Interaction appeared in English natural philosophy, and the adjective interactive followed in the same decade with the sense 'mutually acting'. Early uses described forces, not people or machines.
items.cn: interaction 出现在英语自然哲学中，形容词 interactive 在同一时期跟进，义为“相互作用的”。早期用法描述的是力，而不是人或机器。

items.en: The adjective extended to human relations and to systems, often in the phrase 'interactive effects'. It remained a learned word, commoner in science than in daily speech.
items.cn: 这个形容词扩展到人际关系与系统，常出现在 interactive effects 这一说法中。它长期是学术词，在科学文本中比在日常口语中常见。

items.en: Computer science gave the word its decisive modern sense: a program is interactive if it accepts input and answers during the session. The term separated real-time work from batch processing.
items.cn: 计算机科学赋予这个词决定性的现代义：程序在会话中接受输入并回答，就是交互式的。这个术语把实时工作与批处理区分开来。

items.en: Museums, schools, and broadcasters adopted 'interactive' as a label for audience participation, extending the computer model of input and response to culture and education.
items.cn: 博物馆、学校与广播机构把 interactive 用作观众参与的标签，把输入与回应的计算机模型扩展到文化与教育。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from particle physics to touch screens. In every case the test is the same: does the other side answer, and does the answer change what happens next?
items.cn: 现代用法从粒子物理一直延伸到触摸屏。无论哪种情况，检验标准都一样：另一方是否回应，而回应是否改变接下来的发展？

note.en: The look-alike group separates adjectival forms built on agere with different prefixes; the near-meaning group separates words for responsiveness and participation.
note.cn: 形近组区分以 agere 为词根但前缀不同的形容词；近义组区分表示“有回应”与“可参与”的词。

entries.definition: responding to a stimulus, often chemically. The re- means 'back', so the word stresses reaction after an event rather than exchange between equals.
entries.definitionCN: 对刺激作出反应，常用于化学。re- 意为“回”，因此这个词强调事件之后的反应，而不是对等双方的交流。

entries.definition: not active. Here in- is a negating prefix attached to active; there is no second party and no exchange at all.
entries.definitionCN: 不活跃的。这里的 in- 是否定前缀，加在 active 上；不存在第二方，也完全没有交流。

entries.definition: relating to interaction as a process. It describes the study or structure of exchanges, not a device or person that responds.
entries.definitionCN: 与互动过程有关的。它描述交流的研究或结构，而不是会回应的设备或人。

entries.definition: quick to react to something. It stresses speed and attentiveness on one side; interactive stresses that both sides act.
entries.definitionCN: 反应迅速的。它强调一方的速度与关注；interactive 强调双方都在行动。

entries.definition: allowing movement or communication in both directions. It names the channel, while interactive names the responding behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 允许双向移动或通信的。它命名通道，而 interactive 命名回应行为。

entries.definition: involving people as active participants. It stresses membership and taking part, not the back-and-forth of response.
entries.definitionCN: 让人作为积极参与者的。它强调加入与参与，而不是来回的回应。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the inter- + act pattern, the computing contrast with batch mode, and the everyday phrase interactive display.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：inter- + act 的构词模式、与批处理模式相对的计算机用法，以及日常说法 interactive display。

normal.en: inter- 'between' + act 'do' + -ive: something that keeps doing between two sides.
normal.cn: inter-“在……之间”+ act“做”+ -ive：一直在两方之间做的东西。

normal.en: If the screen answers your finger, it is interactive; if it only shows, it is not.
normal.cn: 屏幕回应你的手指，就是 interactive；只显示不回应，就不是。

normal.en: Batch mode runs alone; interactive mode waits for you — that is the difference the word marks.
normal.cn: 批处理模式独自运行；交互模式等你输入——这个词标记的正是这个差别。

normal.en: An interactive class is measured by how many directions talk travels, not by how loud the teacher is.
normal.cn: 互动课堂按话语传播的方向数来衡量，而不是按老师嗓门大小。

normal.en: An interactive exhibition is unfinished until a visitor touches it.
normal.cn: 互动展览在观众触碰之前都算未完成。

abstract.en: The word describes a loop with two live ends; remove either end and the adjective no longer applies.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述一个两端都活着的回路；去掉任一端，这个形容词就不再适用。

abstract.en: Response is the test: a thing is interactive only if what you do changes what it does next.
abstract.cn: 回应是检验标准：只有你的作为改变了它接下来的作为，它才算 interactive。

abstract.en: From particles to novels, the same shape recurs — action, answer, altered next action.
abstract.cn: 从粒子到小说，同一个形状反复出现——行动、回应、被改变的下一个行动。

examples.en: The museum added interactive exhibits that respond to visitors' movements.
examples.cn: 博物馆增设了能对观众动作作出反应的互动展项。

examples.en: Interactive learning produces more questions than a straight lecture.
examples.cn: 互动式学习比纯讲授产生更多提问。

examples.en: The software runs in interactive mode so users see results at once.
examples.cn: 这款软件以交互模式运行，用户可以立刻看到结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因它来爱克提舞”——它一来，两边就“克”着互动起来 → interactive 互动的、交互式的

root: inter-（在……之间）+ 拉丁语 agere/actum“做”+ -ive（形容词后缀）；字面义“在两者之间来回做的”，核心是“一方动作、另一方回应”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of interactive all describe a loop with two active ends: forces, people, devices, audiences, classes, programs, feedback cycles, and games. The word is a property, not an event — it says that answering is possible.
sensesIntro.cn: interactive 的八个义项都描述一个两端都在活动的回路：力、人、设备、观众、课堂、程序、反馈循环与游戏。这个词是一种属性，而不是一个事件——它说的是“回应是可能的”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger touches a screen and the screen changes at once; action and answer in one moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指触碰屏幕，屏幕立刻改变；动作与回应在同一瞬间。

branches.en: NATURAL PROCESS: forces and feedback cycles act on each other without any user.
branches.cn: 自然过程：力与反馈循环在没有任何使用者的情况下彼此作用。

branches.en: PEOPLE: conversation and two-way teaching depend on alternating turns.
branches.cn: 人：交谈与双向教学依赖轮次的交替。

branches.en: MACHINE: a device or program waits for input and answers it, in contrast with batch operation.
branches.cn: 机器：设备或程序等待输入并回应，与批处理运行相对。

branches.en: AUDIENCE: exhibitions and media invite the visitor to act and then answer that act.
branches.cn: 观众：展览与媒体邀请观众动手，再对这一动作作出回应。

branches.en: PLAY: choices branch the story, so the audience holds authority over the outcome.
branches.cn: 游戏：选择让故事分岔，观众因此对结局拥有决定权。

intro.en: Interactive is interact + -ive, and interact is a back-formation from interaction. The family therefore circles around Latin agere 'to do', with inter- 'between' added in English.
intro.cn: interactive 是 interact + -ive，而 interact 是 interaction 的逆构词。整个家族因此围绕拉丁语 agere“做”，并由英语加上 inter-“在……之间”。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere 'to do, drive' gives actus, actio, activus, and the frequentative agitare. The prefix inter- is a separate preposition; it was attached to English act, not inherited as a Latin compound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere“做、驱动”给出 actus、actio、activus 与反复动词 agitare。前缀 inter- 是独立的介词，它是加在英语 act 上，而不是作为拉丁复合词继承下来的。

items.meaningCN: 以交互方式（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaningCN: 互动性；交互性（-ity 构成抽象名词）

items.meaningCN: 互动程度（-ness 构成抽象名词）

items.meaningCN: 非交互的；单向的（non- 表否定）

senses.title: Combining disciplines in research
senses.definition: describing research that draws methods or data from two or more established fields to answer one question
senses.definitionCN: 描述为回答一个问题而借用两门以上成熟学科的方法或数据的研究
senses.example: The interdisciplinary study combined geology and archaeology to date the eruption.
senses.exampleCN: 这项跨学科研究结合地质学与考古学来确定喷发年代。
senses.why: Interdisciplinary is inter- 'between' plus disciplinary, from Latin disciplina 'instruction, knowledge'. The adjective asserts that a question sits between fields — no single discipline owns it.
senses.whyCN: interdisciplinary 是 inter-“在……之间”加 disciplinary，而后者源自拉丁语 disciplina“教导、知识”。这个形容词主张某个问题处在学科之间——没有哪一门学科独占它。

senses.title: Spanning disciplines in teaching
senses.definition: describing a course or curriculum that teaches content from several fields in one programme
senses.definitionCN: 描述在一门课程或培养方案中教授多个领域内容的课程
senses.example: The university offers an interdisciplinary major in climate and public policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学开设气候与公共政策方向的跨学科专业。
senses.why: Education uses the adjective to describe structure: one timetable, several departments. The word signals that students are expected to move between vocabularies, not to master one.
senses.whyCN: 教育领域用这个形容词描述结构：一张课表，几个院系。这个词表明学生要在不同词汇体系之间移动，而不是精通其中一门。

senses.title: Working across disciplines in a team
senses.definition: describing a group whose members are trained in different fields and share a task
senses.definitionCN: 描述成员受训于不同领域并共担任务的团队
senses.example: An interdisciplinary team of engineers and physicians designed the device.
senses.exampleCN: 由工程师与医生组成的跨学科团队设计了这台设备。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes people rather than knowledge: the team's strength is that no member can read the whole problem alone. The prefix marks the seam between specialisms.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词描述人而不是知识：团队的力量在于没有哪个成员能独自读懂整个问题。前缀标记的正是专业之间的接缝。

senses.title: Borrowing methods across fields
senses.definition: describing an approach that applies the tools or models of one field to the problems of another
senses.definitionCN: 描述把一个领域的工具或模型用于另一个领域问题的做法
senses.example: The paper takes an interdisciplinary approach, using network theory to read historical records.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文采用跨学科方法，用网络理论解读历史记录。
senses.why: The adjective often attaches to 'approach' or 'method', where the borrowing is deliberate rather than accidental. A method becomes interdisciplinary when its assumptions are imported along with its techniques.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常修饰 approach 或 method，那里的借用是有意的而非偶然。当一套方法的假设连同技术一起被引入时，它就变成跨学科的。

senses.title: Naming an emerging field
senses.definition: describing a field that exists only where two or more disciplines overlap, such as bioinformatics
senses.definitionCN: 描述仅在两门或更多学科交叠处存在的领域，如生物信息学
senses.example: Bioinformatics is an interdisciplinary field born from biology and computer science.
senses.exampleCN: 生物信息学是由生物学与计算机科学孕育出的交叉学科领域。
senses.why: When a hybrid field matures, the adjective becomes part of its name. The word then no longer describes a project but a territory that belongs to no single department.
senses.whyCN: 当一个杂交领域成熟时，这个形容词就成为它名字的一部分。此时这个词不再描述一个项目，而描述一块不属于任何单一院系的领地。

senses.title: Institutional cross-department arrangement
senses.definition: describing centres, institutes, or programmes set up to connect departments that normally work apart
senses.definitionCN: 描述为连接通常各自为政的院系而设立的中心、研究所或项目
senses.example: The interdisciplinary centre reports to three faculties at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这个跨学科中心同时向三个学院汇报。
senses.why: Universities invented such units to solve an administrative problem: budgets and appointments sit inside departments, while problems do not. The word names the exception built to cross those walls.
senses.whyCN: 大学发明这类单位是为了解决一个管理难题：预算与人事都在院系内部，而问题不在。这个词命名的是为穿越这些墙而建的例外。

senses.title: An interdisciplinary perspective
senses.definition: describing an analytical view that deliberately holds several disciplinary framings at once
senses.definitionCN: 描述有意同时持有多种学科框架的分析视角
senses.example: Her interdisciplinary reading of the novel draws on economics and theology.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这部小说的跨学科解读借用了经济学与神学。
senses.why: This sense is about seeing, not organising: the analyst keeps two frames active and lets them correct each other. The prefix becomes a way of preventing a single frame from claiming the whole truth.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项关乎“看”，而非“组织”：分析者让两个框架同时工作，并让它们互相纠正。前缀由此成为一种手段，防止单一框架宣称掌握全部真相。

senses.title: Interdisciplinary in a degree or publication
senses.titleCN: 学位或成果的跨学科属性
senses.definition: describing a thesis, journal, or degree formally labelled as spanning more than one discipline
senses.definitionCN: 描述被正式标注为横跨一门以上学科的论文、期刊或学位
senses.example: The dissertation was accepted as interdisciplinary work by a joint committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文被联合委员会接受为跨学科成果。
senses.why: Institutions need labels for evaluation: a joint committee, a mixed methodology, a shared credit. The adjective here is a classification with real consequences for funding and hiring.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要用于评估的标签：联合委员会、混合方法、共享学分。这里的形容词是一种分类，对经费与聘任有实际后果。

intro.en: Interdisciplinary is inter- 'between' plus disciplinary, from Latin disciplina 'teaching, knowledge', itself from discipulus 'pupil' and discere 'to learn'. The compound is a twentieth-century English coinage, not a Latin word.
intro.cn: interdisciplinary 是 inter-“在……之间”加 disciplinary，后者源自拉丁语 disciplina“教导、知识”，而 disciplina 又来自 discipulus“学生”与 discere“学习”。这个复合词是 20 世纪英语的创造，不是拉丁语词。

items.en: Latin discere meant 'to learn'; discipulus 'pupil' and disciplina 'instruction, field of knowledge' came from it. Disciplina already carried both meanings that English still keeps: training and a branch of study.
items.cn: 拉丁语 discere 意为“学习”；discipulus“学生”与 disciplina“教导、知识领域”由此而来。disciplina 已经带有英语仍保留的两重含义：训练与一门学问。

items.en: English discipline entered through Old French with the senses 'instruction', 'a branch of learning', and 'correction'. The punitive sense and the academic sense grew side by side from the same idea of training.
items.cn: 英语 discipline 经古法语进入，义为“教导”“一门学问”“纠正”。惩罚义与学术义从同一个“训练”观念中并肩生长出来。

items.en: The modern research university organized knowledge into departments, and 'discipline' became the word for those units. Boundaries were the point: each field had its own methods and journals.
items.cn: 现代研究型大学把知识组织成系科，discipline 于是成为这些单位的名称。边界正是关键：每个领域有自己的方法与期刊。

items.en: Interdisciplinary is generally dated to the 1920s and 1930s, when foundations and universities began funding work that crossed departments. The exact first use is uncertain, but the coinage is not in doubt.
items.cn: interdisciplinary 一般被认为产生于 1920 至 1930 年代，当时基金会与大学开始资助跨越院系的工作。确切首次使用来源不确定，但属新造词这一点无疑。

items.en: Cold War research projects, area studies, and later environmental science made cross-department work normal. The adjective moved from describing exceptions to naming whole programmes and fields.
items.cn: 冷战时期的研究项目、区域研究以及后来的环境科学使跨系工作成为常态。这个形容词从描述例外，转为命名整个项目与领域。

items.en: Today the word sits beside multidisciplinary and transdisciplinary, each marking a different depth of integration. Interdisciplinary usually means fields cooperate on a shared question while keeping their methods.
items.cn: 今天这个词与 multidisciplinary、transdisciplinary 并列，各自标记不同的整合深度。interdisciplinary 通常指各领域围绕共同问题合作，同时保留各自的方法。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the multi-, cross-, and trans- forms, which differ in how deeply the disciplines are integrated; the near-meaning group separates words for combined and cooperative work.
note.cn: 形近组区分 multi-、cross-、trans- 三种形式，它们的学科整合深度不同；近义组区分表示“结合”与“合作”的词。

entries.definition: involving several disciplines placed next to each other. Multi- 'many' suggests parallel contributions rather than a single fused method, which is weaker integration than interdisciplinary.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及多门学科并置。multi-“多”暗示各学科平行贡献，而不是融合成一套方法，整合程度比 interdisciplinary 弱。

entries.definition: crossing disciplinary boundaries so thoroughly that a new framework is created. Trans- 'across, beyond' marks deeper integration than interdisciplinary.
entries.definitionCN: 如此彻底地穿越学科边界，以致产生新框架。trans-“越过、之外”标记比 interdisciplinary 更深的整合。

entries.definition: relating to a discipline of study, or to correction and punishment. Without inter- it stays inside one field or refers to rules.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一学科有关的，或与惩戒有关的。没有 inter- 时，它仍在一门学科之内，或指规则。

entries.definition: working across the boundaries of disciplines. It is close to interdisciplinary but more often describes a single crossing, such as a team drawn from two departments.
entries.definitionCN: 跨越学科边界工作。它接近 interdisciplinary，但更常描述单次跨越，例如由两个院系组成的团队。

entries.definition: combined into a working whole. It describes the outcome, while interdisciplinary describes the range of fields involved.
entries.definitionCN: 结合成一个可运转的整体。它描述结果，而 interdisciplinary 描述所涉领域的范围。

entries.definition: involving people working together. It names the cooperation itself, not the academic disciplines of the participants.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及人们一起工作的。它命名合作本身，而不是参与者的学科归属。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: inter- 'between' + disciplina 'knowledge', the department walls of the modern university, and the standard phrases interdisciplinary research and interdisciplinary team.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：inter-“在……之间”+ disciplina“知识”、现代大学的院系之墙，以及 interdisciplinary research、interdisciplinary team 等标准说法。

normal.en: inter- means 'between': interdisciplinary work happens in the corridor between two departments, not in either office.
normal.cn: inter- 意为“在……之间”：跨学科工作发生在两个院系之间的走廊里，而不在任何一间办公室。

normal.en: discipline means both 'a field of study' and 'training', so the word is about trained fields meeting.
normal.cn: discipline 既指“一门学问”，也指“训练”，所以这个词讲的是受过训练的领域相遇。

normal.en: A bioinformatics lab is the clearest picture: half computer science, half biology, one room.
normal.cn: 生物信息学实验室是最清楚的画面：一半计算机科学，一半生物学，同一间屋子。

normal.en: If two fields merely sit side by side, say multidisciplinary; if they fuse, say interdisciplinary.
normal.cn: 两门学科只是并排放着，就用 multidisciplinary；如果融合了，就用 interdisciplinary。

normal.en: An interdisciplinary degree is judged by a joint committee because no single department owns it.
normal.cn: 跨学科学位由联合委员会评定，因为没有哪个院系独占它。

abstract.en: The word does not mean 'knowing a little of everything'; it means holding two rigorous methods at once.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是“什么都懂一点”；它指同时持有两套严谨的方法。

abstract.en: Its value is the seam: at the boundary each discipline is forced to explain assumptions it normally hides.
abstract.cn: 它的价值在接缝处：在边界上，每门学科都被迫解释它平时藏起来的假设。

abstract.en: Departments organize knowledge; interdisciplinary work organizes questions, and questions do not respect walls.
abstract.cn: 院系组织知识；跨学科工作组织问题，而问题不尊重围墙。

examples.en: The interdisciplinary project brought together geologists and historians.
examples.cn: 这个跨学科项目把地质学家与历史学家聚到一起。

examples.en: She chose an interdisciplinary major combining economics and environmental science.
examples.cn: 她选择了结合经济学与环境科学的跨学科专业。

examples.en: Interdisciplinary research is often judged by committees drawn from several faculties.
examples.cn: 跨学科研究常由来自多个学院的委员会评审。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因它来，弟子扑来呢”——它一来，几门学科的弟子都扑到一张桌子上 → interdisciplinary 跨学科的

root: inter-（在……之间）+ 拉丁语 discere“学习”/discipulus“学生”/disciplina“教导、学问”+ -ary；字面义“处于学科之间的”，核心是“多门学科围绕同一问题合作”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of interdisciplinary all place a question, course, team, method, field, centre, reading, or degree between established disciplines. The word marks a seam rather than a mixture: fields cooperate while keeping their own standards.
sensesIntro.cn: interdisciplinary 的八个义项都把某个问题、课程、团队、方法、领域、中心、解读或学位放在成熟学科之间。这个词标记的是一条接缝，而不是一锅混合：各领域合作，同时保留各自的标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several classrooms with different subject signs joined by one corridor, all working at one table.
core.cn: 核心意象：几间挂着不同学科牌子的教室由一条走廊连通，共用一张桌子工作。

branches.en: METHOD: research and analysis borrow tools across a boundary while keeping each field's assumptions visible.
branches.cn: 方法：研究与分析跨边界借用工具，同时让每个领域的假设保持可见。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: courses, degrees, and joint committees are formal arrangements for crossing walls.
branches.cn: 制度：课程、学位与联合委员会是为穿墙而设的正式安排。

branches.en: PEOPLE: a team is interdisciplinary when no member can read the whole problem alone.
branches.cn: 人：当没有成员能独自读懂整个问题时，团队就是跨学科的。

branches.en: FIELD: a hybrid subject such as bioinformatics exists only in the overlap.
branches.cn: 领域：生物信息学这类杂交学科只存在于交叠处。

branches.en: PERSPECTIVE: centres and cross-readings keep two frames active so neither claims the whole truth.
branches.cn: 视角：中心与交叉解读让两个框架同时工作，使任何一方都不能宣称掌握全部真相。

intro.en: Interdisciplinary is inter- + disciplinary, and disciplinary is discipline + -ary. Discipline comes from Latin disciplina. The affix set contrasts the multi-, cross-, and trans- variants with the base word.
intro.cn: interdisciplinary 是 inter- + disciplinary，而 disciplinary 是 discipline + -ary。discipline 源自拉丁语 disciplina。词缀组把 multi-、cross-、trans- 各变体与基础词对照起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin disciplina 'instruction, knowledge' derives from discipulus 'pupil', from discere 'to learn'. The older link to docere 'to teach' is generally accepted but the exact derivation is debated, so it is marked as probable rather than certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 disciplina“教导、知识”源自 discipulus“学生”，而 discipulus 又来自 discere“学习”。它与 docere“教”的更早关联一般被认为是成立的，但确切派生过程有争议，因此标为“一般认为”而非确定。

items.meaning: spanning more than one field of study
items.example: The centre runs interdisciplinary research.
items.exampleCN: 这个中心开展跨学科研究。

items.meaning: a field of study; controlled training
items.meaningCN: 学科；纪律；训练（直接借自拉丁名词）
items.example: History is a demanding discipline.
items.exampleCN: 历史学是一门要求很高的学科。

items.meaning: relating to a field or to correction
items.meaningCN: 学科的；纪律的（-ary 构成形容词）
items.example: The paper crosses disciplinary lines.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文跨越学科界线。

items.meaningCN: 严格执行纪律者（-arian 表人）
items.example: The coach was a strict disciplinarian.
items.exampleCN: 这位教练严格执行纪律。

items.meaning: the quality of belonging to a discipline
items.meaningCN: 学科性（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.example: The essay questions traditional disciplinarity.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章质疑传统的学科性。

items.meaning: using several disciplines side by side
items.example: A multidisciplinary panel reviewed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 一个多学科小组评审了这项方案。

items.meaning: crossing disciplines to build a new frame
items.example: Transdisciplinary work dissolves old boundaries.
items.exampleCN: 超学科工作消解旧的边界。

items.example: The grant supports cross-disciplinary teams.
items.exampleCN: 这笔资助支持交叉学科团队。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏训练的；无纪律的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The undisciplined method produced noisy data.
items.exampleCN: 缺乏规范的方法产生了嘈杂的数据。

latinEntries.meaning: instruction, knowledge, a branch of study
teacher; the root is related but the exact path is debated
latinEntries.meaningCN: 教师；词根与 discere 相关，但确切派生路径有争议（来源不确定）

definition_zh: 兴趣；利益；利息；v. 使感兴趣
definition_en: the feeling of wanting to know more about something, an advantage you gain, or money paid for the use of money
core_image: 一个人把头探过桌边，眼睛跟着别人手里的书页一起移动
scene: 少年挤在人群外圈，踮着脚看摊主手上的老式钟表，舍不得走。The bank pays a little interest on that account each month.
sceneCN: 这里 interest 是「兴趣」（第 1 个义项：想知道更多的心情），句意银行每月给那个账户付一点利息，用的是第 2 个义项。画面里的物件：老式钟表、踮起的脚、存折。

pos.zh: 名词：兴趣；利益；利息；股份
动词：使感兴趣；引起（某人）注意

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「有趣的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「感兴趣的」
由 interesting 加 -ly 构成，义为「有趣的是」
由否定前缀 dis- 加过去分词构成，义为「不带私利的」

senses.title: Wanting to know more
senses.definition: a feeling of curiosity or attention that makes you want to know more about something
senses.definitionCN: 一种好奇或注意的心情，使你想对某事了解更多
senses.example: His interest in old watches began at a street market.
senses.exampleCN: 他对旧钟表的兴趣始于一个街头小市集。
senses.why: Latin interest means "it is between", that is, it makes a difference to someone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 interest 意为「它在其间」，即与人有关、对人有差别。

senses.title: Money paid for money
senses.definition: the money that a borrower pays to a lender for the use of the money over time
senses.definitionCN: 借用人因使用这笔钱而按时间付给放款人的钱
senses.example: A small loan at seven per cent interest adds up quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 百分之七利率的小额贷款很快就滚出不少钱。
senses.why: Roman law made it profitable to have a stake in a loan, and interest came to mean that stake.
senses.whyCN: 罗马法使在借贷中占一份成为有利可图之事，interest 遂指这「一份」。

senses.title: What is good for you
senses.definition: the advantage or benefit of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体的好处与得益
senses.example: The road was closed in the interest of safety.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路为了安全而被封闭。
senses.why: What makes a difference to you is also what serves your advantage.
senses.whyCN: 对你有差别的事，也就是对你有利的事。

senses.title: A share in a business
senses.definition: a legal share or stake in a company or property
senses.definitionCN: 在公司或财产中的合法份额
senses.example: She sold her interest in the shop to her partner.
senses.exampleCN: 她把店里的股份卖给了合伙人。
senses.why: From a stake in a loan the word widened to any ownership share.
senses.whyCN: 从借贷中的一份，此词扩展到任何所有权份额。

senses.title: To draw attention
senses.definition: to make someone want to know or take part
senses.definitionCN: 使某人想了解或参与
senses.example: The teacher interested the class in the old maps on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 老师让全班对墙上的旧地图产生了兴趣。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: it plants the curiosity instead of feeling it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词反过来用：不是产生好奇，而是种下好奇。

intro.en: Interest began as the Latin verb phrase interest "it makes a difference", from inter and esse "to be".
intro.cn: interest 起初是拉丁语动词短语 interest「与之有关」，由 inter 与 esse「存在」构成。

items.en: Interest is literally "it is between", used in phrases like interest reipublicae, it matters to the state.
items.cn: interest 字面是「它在中间」，见于 interest reipublicae 等短语，意谓对国家有干系。

items.en: Roman law compensated a lender for the delay in repayment, weighing what it mattered to him.
items.cn: 罗马法就延迟还款补偿放款人，衡量的正是此事对他有多大干系。

items.en: French interest narrowed to mean money paid for the use of money.
items.cn: 法语 interest 窄化为为使用金钱而付的钱。

items.en: English took interest in the sixteenth century for both money and advantage.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 interest，兼指利息与好处。

items.en: The sense of curiosity appeared later and became the commonest use of all.
items.cn: 「好奇」这一义项较晚出现，却成了最常见用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb esse "to be"; the near-meaning group holds other words for attention and money.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语动词 esse「存在」；近义组收表示注意与钱财的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for things that hold attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容能吸引注意的事物。

entries.definition: The adjective for the person who feels interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容感到兴趣的人。

entries.definition: Free from personal gain, not merely bored.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无利害关系的」，并非「不感兴趣」。

entries.definition: The wish to know, without any stake.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「好奇心」，不带利益。

entries.definition: An advantage, especially as a right.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「益处」，尤指应得的权利。

entries.definition: Money made from a business after costs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「利润」，扣除成本后的所赚。

normalIntro.en: The hooks run from the phrase "it matters to me" to the exact phrases interest lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从「这事与我有关」一路走到 interest 的真实搭配。

normal.en: Interest first meant "it is between": it stands between a person and a thing.
normal.cn: interest 最早意为「在其中间」：站在人与事物之间。

normal.en: Be interested in a topic, take an interest in a hobby.
normal.cn: 对话题用 be interested in，对爱好用 take an interest in。

normal.en: Interest on a loan is your stake in the lender's delay.
normal.cn: 贷款的利息就是你对放款人拖延所占的那一份。

normal.en: In the interest of safety, the road was closed.
normal.cn: 为了安全，这条路被封闭。

normal.en: A conflict of interest means two gains pull against each other.
normal.cn: 利益冲突指的是两份好处互相拉扯。

abstract.en: Interest is the thread that ties attention to advantage.
abstract.cn: 兴趣是把注意力与好处系在一起的那根线。

abstract.en: Money grows by interest; the mind grows by interest too.
abstract.cn: 钱靠利息增长，心也靠兴趣增长。

abstract.en: What matters to you will always hold your eyes.
abstract.cn: 与你有关的事总会牵住你的眼睛。

examples.en: Her interest in birds began with a single nest outside the window.
examples.cn: 她对鸟的兴趣始于窗外的一个鸟巢。

examples.en: The loan is repaid with interest over five years.
examples.cn: 这笔贷款在五年内连本带息还清。

examples.en: He acted in the interest of the whole village, not himself.
examples.cn: 他是为整个村子而非自己行事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因戳瑞斯特」——因被戳到痒处，立刻来了兴趣

root: 拉丁语 inter「在……之间」+ esse「存在」→ 动词短语 interest「与之有关」→ 古法语 interest → 英语 interest。同族：interesting、interested。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: curiosity, money for money, advantage, a share in a business, and the verb of arousing curiosity.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：好奇、钱生钱的利息、好处、生意里的份额，以及使人上心的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person leaning forward, eyes following someone else's book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人探身向前，眼睛跟着别人手里的书走。

branches.en: THE MARKET STALL: curiosity makes the boy stop walking.
branches.cn: 小摊这条线：好奇心让少年停住脚。

branches.en: THE SAVINGS BOOK: money earns money over time.
branches.cn: 存折这条线：钱随时间再生钱。

branches.en: THE CLOSED ROAD: a benefit is weighed against a cost.
branches.cn: 封闭的路这条线：好处要与代价权衡。

branches.en: THE SOLD SHARE: ownership is the same stake in property.
branches.cn: 卖出的股份这条线：所有权即财产中的一份。

branches.en: THE OLD MAPS: a teacher plants the curiosity.
branches.cn: 旧地图这条线：老师把好奇种下去。

intro.en: Interest has no living prefix-and-suffix split in English: it is frozen Latin, inter "between" plus the verb "to be".
intro.cn: interest 在英语里已无活的词缀可分，是一块冻结的拉丁语：inter「在……之间」加「存在」动词。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 interest 与短语 interest reipublicae 均有记载，只有最深的印欧层是重构。

definition_zh: 界面；接口；接触面；相互作用；连接
definition_en: a surface or point where two things meet, or the means by which a user or system communicates with another
core_image: 两块不同的材料在一条清晰的分界线上贴合，一侧是金属，一侧是液体，交界处微微泛起反应的光
scene: 设计师把按钮、搜索框和图标排在一屏之内，用户手指一点就能完成操作。A clear interface makes the software feel simple.
sceneCN: 这里指用户与软件之间交互的屏幕层（第 1 个义项：人机界面）；句意：清晰的界面让软件用起来很简单。

pos.zh: 界面；接口；接触面；相互作用
连接；对接

derivatives.zh: 由该名词加表示「属于」的形容词尾构成，义为「界面的、界面上的」
由该动词加动作词尾构成，义为「对接；对接的」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已对接的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在界面层面」

senses.title: The screen between user and machine
senses.titleCN: 用户与机器之间的屏幕层
senses.definition: the part of a system that a person sees and operates, such as buttons, menus and windows
senses.definitionCN: 系统中被人看见并操作的部分，如按钮、菜单与窗口
senses.example: The interface puts the search box at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 这个界面把搜索框放在页面顶部。
senses.why: The word names the meeting surface, and in software that surface is what the user touches.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名相接的表面，在软件中那个表面就是用户所触的部分。

senses.title: The point where two systems join
senses.definition: a standard connection through which one system or component talks to another
senses.definitionCN: 一个系统或组件与另一个对话时所依据的标准连接
senses.example: The two programs share a narrow interface.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个程序共用一个窄接口。
senses.why: Two systems meet at a defined boundary, and the standards at that boundary are called the interface.
senses.whyCN: 两个系统在一条明确的边界相接，边界上的标准就称为接口。

senses.title: The boundary between two materials
senses.titleCN: 两种材料之间的分界面
senses.definition: the surface where two substances or phases meet
senses.definitionCN: 两种物质或物相相接的表面
senses.example: Water and oil form a sharp interface.
senses.exampleCN: 水与油形成清晰的界面。
senses.why: In physics the word keeps its literal sense: a surface where one phase ends and another begins.
senses.whyCN: 在物理学中这个词保留字面义：一种物相结束、另一种开始的表面。

senses.title: The joint between two parts
senses.titleCN: 两个部件之间的接合处
senses.definition: the place where two machine parts or structures meet and act on each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个机械部件或结构相接并相互作用的位置
senses.example: Engineers checked the interface for wear.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查了接合处是否磨损。
senses.why: Machines also have meeting surfaces where force is transferred, so the word extends to mechanical joints.
senses.whyCN: 机器同样有传递力的相接表面，因此这个词扩展到机械接合处。

senses.title: The channel of interaction
senses.definition: the means by which two parties or fields interact and exchange influence
senses.definitionCN: 两方或两个领域相互作用、交换影响的方式
senses.example: The conference became an interface between research and industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这场会议成了研究与产业之间的交流通道。
senses.why: If two worlds meet, the meeting surface can be social or institutional, not only physical.
senses.whyCN: 若两个世界相遇，相接的表面可以是社会的或机构的，而不只是物理的。

senses.title: The agreed protocol
senses.definition: a documented set of rules that lets independently built systems work together
senses.definitionCN: 一套成文规则，使独立构建的系统能够协同工作
senses.example: The interface is published so other teams can build on it.
senses.exampleCN: 接口规范已公布，其他团队可以据此开发。
senses.why: A boundary needs rules if both sides are built separately, and the rules themselves take the name.
senses.whyCN: 若两侧分别构建，边界就需要规则，而这些规则本身也沿用这个名称。

senses.title: The graphical front end
senses.definition: a visual interface built from windows, icons and pointers rather than typed commands
senses.definitionCN: 由窗口、图标与指针构成、而非键入命令的视觉界面
senses.example: The graphical interface replaced the command line for most users.
senses.exampleCN: 对多数用户而言，图形界面取代了命令行。
senses.why: Drawing rather than typing changes the meeting surface, so the graphical kind gets its own label.
senses.whyCN: 用画而不是打字改变了相接的表面，因此图形化的那一类有了自己的标签。

senses.title: To join two systems
senses.titleCN: 作为动词：使两系统对接
senses.definition: to connect one system or device to another so that they can work together
senses.definitionCN: 把一个系统或设备接到另一个上，使它们协同工作
senses.example: The clinic interface the new records system with the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把新的病历系统与旧系统对接起来。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to create such a meeting surface, a common shift in technical English.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词转为动词，意为建立这样一个相接表面，这是技术英语中常见的转类。

intro.en: Interface is Latin inter, between, plus English face from Latin facies, a form or surface; the computing sense is twentieth-century.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「在……之间」与英语「面」（源自拉丁语「外形、表面」）构成；计算机义项是二十世纪的。

items.en: Inter meant between, and it marks the word as naming something that lies between two sides.
items.cn: 这个词素意为「在……之间」，标记该词命名位于两侧之间的东西。

items.en: Facies meant form, appearance or surface, and it is the source of English face.
items.cn: 这个词意为外形、外观或表面，是英语「面」的来源。

items.en: The noun was coined for the surface where two bodies or phases meet, a sense still used in chemistry and physics.
items.cn: 这个名词最初指两个物体或物相相接的表面，这一义项至今仍用于化学与物理。

items.en: In the 1960s the word was applied to the boundary between hardware and software, and then to what a user sees.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代，这个词被用于硬件与软件的边界，随后又指用户所看到的部分。

items.en: Engineers turned the noun into a verb meaning to connect systems at such a boundary.
items.cn: 工程师把这个名词转为动词，意为在这样的边界上连接系统。

items.en: The first use of the computing sense is often dated to the 1960s, but the exact paper and author are not settled.
items.cn: 计算机义项的首见常被定在二十世纪六十年代，但确切文献与作者尚无定论。

note.en: The first group shares the face or boundary idea; the second group names other meeting points between systems.
note.cn: 第一组共享「面」或「边界」的概念；第二组是系统之间其他类型的相接点。

entries.definition: Relating to a boundary between phases; it describes the surface rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 与物相之间的边界有关的；描述该表面，而不是命名它。

entries.definition: The outer face of a body; the target word adds the idea of lying between two bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 物体的外表面；目标词加上「位于两物之间」的意思。

entries.definition: The front or outer side; it is the English descendant of the Latin word inside interface.
entries.definitionCN: 正面或外侧；是目标词内部那个拉丁词的英语后裔。

entries.definition: The act of joining systems; it names the process rather than the boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 把系统连接起来的动作；命名过程而不是边界。

entries.definition: A line that separates two regions; it is wider and does not imply interaction.
entries.definitionCN: 分隔两个区域的界线；范围更宽，且不暗示相互作用。

entries.definition: A point that admits traffic into another network; a functional kind of interface.
entries.definitionCN: 让流量进入另一网络的入口；是一种功能性的接口。

entries.definition: A single page that gathers access to many services; it is a user-facing entry point, not a boundary standard.
entries.definitionCN: 汇集多种服务入口的单一页面；是面向用户的入口，而非边界标准。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real Latin pieces and the modern technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实拉丁成分与现代技术搭配。

normal.en: Inter means between and face means surface: the surface between two sides.
normal.cn: 「之间」加「面」，就是两侧之间的那个面。

normal.en: The family runs interface, interfacial, interfacing and interfaced.
normal.cn: 同族词有界面、界面的、对接与已对接的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the user side: user interface and graphical user interface.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用户一侧：用户界面与图形用户界面。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the system side: application programming interface, interface design.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出系统一侧：应用程序编程接口、界面设计。

normal.en: Chemistry keeps the oldest sense: the sharp line where water meets oil.
normal.cn: 化学保留了最古老的义项：水与油相接的那条清晰界线。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway that belongs to neither room but serves both.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，不属于任何一个房间，却为两边服务。

abstract.en: Picture two languages agreeing on a single hand signal at a border.
abstract.cn: 想象两种语言在边境约定同一个手势。

abstract.en: Picture a membrane through which two liquids exchange a single colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一层薄膜，两种液体隔着它交换一种颜色。

examples.en: The interface hides the complexity of the database behind simple buttons.
examples.cn: 界面用简单的按钮把数据库的复杂性藏了起来。

examples.en: A well-documented interface lets two teams work independently.
examples.cn: 一个有良好文档的接口让两个团队可以独立工作。

examples.en: The study examined the interface between climate and agriculture.
examples.cn: 这项研究考察了气候与农业之间的相互作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特面」——互联网之间的那个面 → 界面、接口

root: 拉丁语「在……之间」加拉丁语「外形、表面」；十九世纪末指两物的交界面。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a meeting surface: user screen, system boundary, material boundary, mechanical joint, channel of interaction, agreed protocol, graphical front end, and the verb of joining.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指一个相接表面：用户屏幕、系统边界、材料分界、机械接合、交流通道、约定规范、图形前端，以及表示连接的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear line where two different sides touch and exchange something.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条清晰的界线，两侧不同的事物在此相触并交换某物。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE MEETING SURFACE: what a user sees, including the graphical version built from windows and icons.
branches.cn: 可见的相接表面：用户所见的部分，包括由窗口与图标构成的图形版本。

branches.en: THE RULED BOUNDARY: the standard connection and the documented rules that let separate systems work together.
branches.cn: 有规则的边界：标准连接与成文规则，使彼此独立的系统协同工作。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BOUNDARY: where two materials or machine parts meet.
branches.cn: 物理边界：两种材料或机械部件相接之处。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL CHANNEL: a meeting surface between fields, institutions or groups.
branches.cn: 社会通道：领域、机构或群体之间的相接表面。

branches.en: THE ACT OF JOINING: turning the meeting surface into a working connection.
branches.cn: 连接的动作：把相接表面变成可工作的连接。

intro.en: Interface is a hybrid of a Latin prefix and an English noun of Latin origin; both parts still build words.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁前缀与源自拉丁语的英语名词的混合体；两部分至今都在构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the prefix inter and the noun facies behind face, so real cognates appear in the list.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了前缀「之间」与「面」背后的名词，因此列表中列出真实同族词。

items.example: The prefix places the surface between two sides.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把该表面放在两侧之间。

items.example: The second half supplies the surface in the image.
items.exampleCN: 后半提供了画面中的那个表面。

items.example: The Latin noun stands behind the English face.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是英语「面」的来源。

items.example: The noun first named a physical boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初指物理边界。

items.example: Interfacial describes what happens at the boundary.
items.exampleCN: 「界面的」描述边界上发生的事。

items.example: Interfacing is the work of making systems talk.
items.exampleCN: 「对接」是让系统对话的工作。

items.example: The interfaced modules share one clock.
items.exampleCN: 已对接的模块共享一个时钟。

items.meaning: the outer face of a body
items.example: Surface is the everyday word for one side of the boundary.
items.exampleCN: 「表面」是边界一侧的日常说法。

derivatives.zh: 由该名词加表示「属于」的形容词尾构成，义为「界面的、界面上的」
由该动词加动作词尾构成，义为「对接；对接的」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已对接的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在界面层面」

definition_zh: 干涉；妨碍；干扰
definition_en: to become involved in something in a way that is not wanted, or to disturb what is happening
core_image: 一只手伸进两台正在咬合的齿轮之间，把事情搅乱
scene: 两个人在谈事情，第三个人忽然插进来替其中一人作答。Please do not interfere while the machine is being repaired.
sceneCN: 这里 interfere 是「干涉、妨碍」（第 1 个义项：以不受欢迎的方式介入），句意机器正在修理，请勿干扰。画面里的物件：齿轮、插话的第三人、修理工具。

pos.zh: 动词：干涉；妨碍；干扰

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ence 构成，义为「干涉；干扰」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「爱管闲事的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「干涉者」
由否定前缀 non- 加本词构成，义为「不干涉」

senses.title: Meddle in others' affairs
senses.definition: to take part in something that is not your business, often with unwelcome results
senses.definitionCN: 参与本不归你管的事，常常带来不受欢迎的后果
senses.example: The neighbours interfered in the argument and made it worse.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们插手这场争吵，反而让它更糟。
senses.why: Latin ferire means to strike; interferire is to strike in between two things.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ferire 意为「击打」，interferire 即「在两者之间打进去」。

senses.title: Disturb or hinder
senses.definition: to hinder or disturb a process, signal, or activity that was working well
senses.definitionCN: 妨碍或扰乱原本进行良好的过程、信号或活动
senses.example: Bright lights interfere with the sensor.
senses.exampleCN: 强光会干扰传感器。
senses.why: Radio engineers took the verb up because one wave can strike across another.
senses.whyCN: 无线电工程师采用了这个动词，因为一束波会横穿过另一束。

senses.title: Touch what is not yours
senses.definition: to touch or handle something that you should leave alone, especially in a harmful way
senses.definitionCN: 触碰或摆弄本该不动的某物，尤指造成损害
senses.example: Do not let anyone interfere with the wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 别让任何人动那套线路。
senses.why: The original physical sense survives where hands actually meddle with objects.
senses.whyCN: 在最原始的身体意义上，这个词指手真的去碰东西。

intro.en: Interfere combines inter- "between" with the Latin verb ferire "to strike".
intro.cn: interfere 把 inter-「在……之间」与拉丁语动词 ferire「击打」结合在一起。

items.en: Ferire "to strike" was common in Latin for blows and struck deals.
items.cn: ferire「击打」在拉丁语中常见于「打」与「成交」的说法。

items.en: Interferire was rare and meant to come between with a blow.
items.cn: interferire 很少见，意为「用一击插到中间」。

items.en: French s'entreférir carried the idea of clashing or hitting against.
items.cn: 法语 s'entreférir 带有相撞、对冲的意思。

items.en: English first used interfere of horses striking their hooves together.
items.cn: 英语早期用 interfere 形容马匹的蹄子相撞。

items.en: The sense shifted to getting in the way, then to meddling in other's affairs.
items.cn: 意义转向「挡路」，再转向「插手别人的事」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the striking root; the near-meaning group holds other words for getting in the way.
note.cn: 形近组共享「击打」词根；近义组收其他表示「妨碍」的词。

entries.definition: The noun for meddling or for unwanted signal noise.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「干涉」或「干扰噪声」。

entries.definition: To work out a conclusion from evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推断」，由证据推出结论。

entries.definition: To bury a body in the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「埋葬」。

entries.definition: To busy oneself with what is not one's business.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「瞎掺和」，专指管闲事。

entries.definition: To break the calm or order of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打扰」，打破平静或秩序。

entries.definition: To block a path or process physically.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「阻碍」，以物理方式挡住。

normalIntro.en: The hooks build on ferire, the blow hidden in the middle of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子建立在词中间藏着的 ferire「击打」上。

normal.en: Inter plus ferire: strike in between, and the gears jam.
normal.cn: inter 加 ferire：在中间打一记，齿轮就卡住了。

normal.en: Interfere with a plan, interfere in a quarrel.
normal.cn: 打乱计划用 with，插手争吵用 in。

normal.en: Static interferes with the radio signal.
normal.cn: 静电干扰无线电信号。

normal.en: Good parents watch, but do not interfere.
normal.cn: 好的父母看着，但不插手。

normal.en: Two interfering neighbours can spoil a quiet street.
normal.cn: 两个爱插手的邻居能毁掉安静的街道。

abstract.en: Help offered unasked can turn into interference.
abstract.cn: 未被请求的帮助会变成干涉。

abstract.en: Every blow struck between two things leaves a mark.
abstract.cn: 打在两物之间的每一击都会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Some things grow best when nobody interferes.
abstract.cn: 有些东西在无人插手下才长得好。

examples.en: Parents should not interfere in their grown children's careers.
examples.cn: 父母不应干涉成年子女的职业选择。

examples.en: The new building may interfere with television reception.
examples.cn: 新楼可能会干扰电视信号。

examples.en: Wind interfered with the firefighting planes all afternoon.
examples.cn: 大风整个下午都妨碍着消防飞机作业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特费尔」——网上特费劲，因为总有人来干扰

root: 拉丁语 ferire「击打」→ inter-「在……之间」+ ferire → interferire「打进去」→ 古法语 s'entreférir → 英语 interfere。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: meddling in others' business, disturbing a process, and handling what should be left alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：插手别人的事、妨碍某个过程，以及乱动不该动的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching into interlocking gears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸进正咬合的齿轮之间。

branches.en: THE THREE TALKERS: the third voice breaks into a private talk.
branches.cn: 三人谈话这条线：第三个声音闯入私下的谈话。

branches.en: THE SENSOR: another light blinds the signal.
branches.cn: 传感器这条线：另一束光把信号晃瞎。

branches.en: THE WIRING: idle hands spoil a careful job.
branches.cn: 线路这条线：闲手毁掉细致的活儿。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses bring harm from the wrong place.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都是从错误位置带来的损害。

branches.en: THE LINK: disturbing objects is one way of meddling.
branches.cn: 连接线：乱动东西就是插手的一种。

intro.en: Interfere = inter- "between" + fer- "strike" + -e, the Latin verb ending.
intro.cn: interfere = inter-「在……之间」+ fer-「击打」+ -e（拉丁动词词尾）。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferire and the rare interferire are recorded, if thinly attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ferire 与少见的 interferire 有记载，尽管材料不多。

items.example: It places the blow in the middle.
items.exampleCN: 它把这一击放到中间。

items.example: Also in ferocious, loosely related.
items.exampleCN: 也见于 ferocious，关联较远。

items.exampleCN: 合成词的基础动词。

items.example: The direct source of the French form.
items.exampleCN: 法语形式的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 interference。

items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词 interfering。

definition_zh: 内部；里面；adj. 内部的；内地的
definition_en: the inside part of something, or relating to the inside
core_image: 从窗外看进去，屋里亮着灯，家具的轮廓清清楚楚
scene: 车停在路边，雨刷还在动，车内仪表盘泛着微光。The interior of the old church is darker than the square outside.
sceneCN: 这里 interior 是「内部、里面」（第 1 个义项：某物的内侧空间），句意这座老教堂内部比外面广场更暗。画面里的物件：车内仪表盘、教堂穹顶、窗外的光。

pos.zh: 名词：内部；里面；内地；内政
形容词：内部的；内地的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ize 构成，义为「内化」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在内部」
由同一词干构成，义为「内部的」
由相反方向的前缀构成，义为「外部」

senses.title: The inside space
senses.definition: the inside part of a building, room, or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、房间或车辆内部的那部分
senses.example: The interior of the van smelled of new paint.
senses.exampleCN: 货车内部有一股新油漆味。
senses.why: Latin interior is the comparative of the adjective meaning "inner".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 interior 是意为「内部的」形容词的比较级。

senses.title: The land far from the coast
senses.definition: the central part of a country, away from the sea and borders
senses.definitionCN: 一国的中心部分，远离海岸与边境
senses.example: Traders carried salt far into the interior.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们运盐深入内陆。
senses.why: Explorers spoke of the interior because maps stopped at the coast.
senses.whyCN: 航海者谈「内陆」，因为地图止于海岸线。

senses.title: The inside story
senses.definition: the part of a person or a thing that is not shown outwardly
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物不外露的那部分
senses.example: Her calm voice hid a troubled interior.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的声音下藏着不安的内心。
senses.why: The spatial word moves inward to name hidden feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这个空间词向内延伸，用来指隐藏的感受。

senses.title: Home affairs
senses.definition: the domestic affairs of a country as opposed to its foreign policy
senses.definitionCN: 一国的国内事务，与外交政策相对
senses.example: The interior minister promised tighter border checks.
senses.exampleCN: 内政部长承诺加强边境检查。
senses.why: Governments name domestic affairs by the word for inside space.
senses.whyCN: 政府用表示内部空间的词来命名国内事务。

intro.en: Interior is the Latin comparative of an inner adjective; it came to English as both noun and adjective.
intro.cn: interior 是拉丁语中表示「内部的」形容词的比较级，作为名词与形容词一同进入英语。

items.en: The preposition inter "among" gave rise to an adjective for what lies inside.
items.cn: 介词 inter「在……之中」生出一个指「在里面」的形容词。

items.en: Interior was its comparative, meaning more inside, as in "interior pars".
items.cn: interior 是它的比较级，意为「更靠里的」，如 interior pars。

items.en: Writers used interior for the inner area of a land or a house.
items.cn: 作家用 interior 指土地或房舍的里侧区域。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century as an adjective.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪先把它作形容词借入。

items.en: The noun spread to mean innermost land, inner rooms, and finally private feeling.
items.cn: 名词随后扩展到「内陆」「内室」，乃至私人的内心。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the inner root; the near-meaning group holds other words for the inside.
note.cn: 形近组共享「内部」词根；近义组收其他表示内部的词。

entries.definition: Inside an organisation or a body.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「内部的」，指组织或身体之内。

entries.definition: The outside surface, the exact opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「外部」，正好相反。

entries.definition: In the inner part; rare but real.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在内部」，少见但真实。

entries.definition: The everyday word for what is within.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「里面」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: The country's middle, away from the coast.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「内陆的」。

entries.definition: Of the home, or of affairs inside a country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「家庭的；国内的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the comparison hidden in interior and the places it is used.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用 interior 中藏着的比较意味，并挂上它常用的场合。

normal.en: Interior is the more inside one, the comparative of inner.
normal.cn: interior 是「更靠里的那个」，即「内部」的比较级。

normal.en: Interior design works on the inside of rooms.
normal.cn: 室内设计做的是房间的内侧。

normal.en: Explorers carried salt into the interior.
normal.cn: 探险者把盐运进内陆。

normal.en: The interior ministry handles borders and police.
normal.cn: 内政部管边境与警察。

normal.en: A calm face can hide an uncertain interior.
normal.cn: 平静的面容可以掩盖不确定的内心。

abstract.en: The word turns a country into a house with a middle.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一个国家变成有里屋的房子。

abstract.en: Interior is a compass pointing inward.
abstract.cn: interior 是一只指向内侧的罗盘。

abstract.en: Some journeys into the interior never cross a border.
abstract.cn: 有些走向内陆的旅程从不过境。

examples.en: The interior of the theatre was painted deep red.
examples.cn: 剧院内部漆成了深红色。

examples.en: Rain rarely reaches the dry interior of the island.
examples.cn: 雨水很少落到岛上干旱的内陆。

examples.en: He spoke calmly, but his interior was in turmoil.
examples.cn: 他语气平静，内心却一片混乱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特瑞尔」——网上的内容都在里面，所以是内部

root: 拉丁语 inter「在……之中」→ 形容词 inner 族 → 比较级 interior「更靠里的」→ 英语 interior。反义：exterior。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: inner space, inland regions, hidden feeling, and home affairs.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：内部空间、内陆地区、隐藏的感受，以及国内政务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room seen through a window at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里透过窗户看见一间亮着灯的房间。

branches.en: THE VAN: the inside is a separate space from the street.
branches.cn: 货车这条线：内部是与街道分开的一处空间。

branches.en: THE SALT TRADERS: the map continues past the coast.
branches.cn: 盐商这条线：地图越过海岸继续延伸。

branches.en: THE CALM VOICE: the inward room of a person.
branches.cn: 平静声音这条线：人里面的那间屋子。

branches.en: THE MINISTRY: a nation is imagined as a house.
branches.cn: 内阁这条线：国家被想象成一座房子。

branches.en: THE LINK: politics borrows the house metaphor.
branches.cn: 连接线：政治借用了房子的比喻。

intro.en: Interior = inter- "among" + the comparative ending -ior, literally "more within".
intro.cn: interior = inter-「在……之中」+ 比较级词尾 -ior，字面即「更在里面的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin interior is attested as both adjective and noun; the ending -ior is the Latin comparative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 interior 作形容词与名词均有记载，-ior 是拉丁比较级词尾。

items.example: It anchors the word inside.
items.exampleCN: 它把词锚定在内部。

items.example: It makes "more inside" out of "inside".
items.exampleCN: 它把「在里面」变成「更在里面」。

items.example: It appears in interiority.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 interiority 中。

items.example: It forms interiorize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 interiorize。

items.example: It forms interiorly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 interiorly。

items.example: It builds the opposite exterior.
items.exampleCN: 它造出反义的 exterior。

items.example: A near twin with a different ending.
items.exampleCN: 另一个同源近亲，词尾不同。

items.example: Same root, a physical sense.
items.exampleCN: 同根，取身体意义。

definition_zh: 中间的；中级的；n. 中间物；中级学习者
definition_en: coming between two things in level or position, or a person at a middle stage of learning
core_image: 三段楼梯中间的第三级台阶上放着一盏灯，上下各有台阶
scene: 语言班门口挂着一块牌子，把班级分成初级、中级、高级三栏。She moved from the beginner class to an intermediate one in a term.
sceneCN: 这里 intermediate 是「中级的」（第 1 个义项：处于两端之间），句意她一个学期就从初级班升到了中级班。画面里的物件：班级分栏牌、台阶、课本。

pos.zh: 形容词：中间的；中级的；中等的
名词：中间物；中级学习者

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「居间调解；中介」
由同一词干构成，义为「中间人」
去掉前缀 inter- 的直接对照词，义为「立即的；直接的」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「调解者」

senses.title: In the middle of a scale
senses.definition: at a level between the basic and the advanced
senses.definitionCN: 处于基础与高级之间的水平
senses.example: The book is written for intermediate learners of English.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是为中级英语学习者写的。
senses.why: The Latin stem medius "middle" with inter- marks a point between two ends.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词干 medius「中间」与 inter- 相合，标出介于两端之间的点。

senses.title: Between two stages or places
senses.definition: happening or lying between two other things in time or space
senses.definitionCN: 在时间或位置上位于另外两事之间
senses.example: The larva spends several weeks in an intermediate stage.
senses.exampleCN: 幼虫在中间阶段要经过好几周。
senses.why: Latin medius "middle" with inter- marks a point that is in between.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 medius「中间」与 inter- 相合，标出介于两者之间的点。

senses.title: Not directly connected
senses.definition: happening through an extra step rather than directly
senses.definitionCN: 经由额外一步而非直接地发生
senses.example: The sugar is broken down into intermediate products first.
senses.exampleCN: 糖先被分解成中间产物。
senses.why: Chemistry and economics both need names for halfway results.
senses.whyCN: 化学与经济学都需要为半途的产物命名。

senses.title: A person at that level
senses.definition: a learner or athlete who is no longer a beginner but not yet advanced
senses.definitionCN: 已不是新手但尚未达到高水平的学练者
senses.example: The class mixes intermediates with a few beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班以中级学员为主，也混着几个新手。
senses.why: The adjective turned into a noun for people in the middle band.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词活用作名词，指处在中间一档的人。

intro.en: Intermediate joins Latin inter- "between" to medius "middle", with the adjective ending -ate.
intro.cn: intermediate 把拉丁语 inter-「在……之间」接到 medius「中间」上，再加形容词词尾 -ate。

items.en: Medius means middle, and gives English medium and mediate.
items.cn: medius 意为「中间的」，给出英语 medium 与 mediate。

items.en: Mediatus, the participle of mediare "to be in the middle", supplied the ending.
items.cn: mediare「居于中间」的分词 mediatus 提供了词尾。

items.en: Intermediatus named what lies between two stages.
items.cn: intermediatus 指位于两个阶段之间之物。

items.en: English adopted intermediate for space, then for levels of skill.
items.cn: 英语先用 intermediate 指空间，再指技能等级。

items.en: Schools and exams fixed it as the band between beginner and advanced.
items.cn: 学校与考试把它固定为初级与高级之间的那一档。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the middle root medius; the near-meaning group holds other words for middleness.
note.cn: 形近组共享「中间」词根 medius；近义组收其他表示居中的词。

entries.definition: With nothing in between, hence instant.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「立即的、直接的」。

entries.definition: A person or body that goes between others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「中间人」。

entries.definition: A middle size, or a means of communication.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「中号」或「媒介」。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the central part.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，最日常的「中间」。

entries.definition: Neither great nor small; not extreme.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「适中的」，不极端。

entries.definition: Belonging to a period of change between two states.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「过渡的」，处于变化之中。

normalIntro.en: The hooks split the word into inter- and media, the Latin middle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词分成 inter- 与拉丁语表示「中间」的 media。

normal.en: Inter plus media: between the middles, that is, in the middle.
normal.cn: inter 加 media：在中间之中，也就是居中。

normal.en: Beginner, intermediate, advanced: three steps on one stair.
normal.cn: 初级、中级、高级：一道楼梯上的三级。

normal.en: An intermediate stage stands between egg and adult.
normal.cn: 中间阶段站在卵与成虫之间。

normal.en: Immediate has no middle; intermediate is all middle.
normal.cn: immediate 没有中间，intermediate 全是中间。

normal.en: Upper intermediate is still not advanced.
normal.cn: 中高级仍不算高级。

abstract.en: The middle step carries the weight of both directions.
abstract.cn: 中间那级台阶承担着两个方向的重量。

abstract.en: Some things are only ever intermediate, never final.
abstract.cn: 有些东西永远是中途，从不到终点。

abstract.en: Being intermediate is a place to stand, not a verdict.
abstract.cn: 处在中游是一个立足处，不是判决。

examples.en: She joined an intermediate swimming class at fourteen.
examples.cn: 她十四岁时参加了中级游泳班。

examples.en: The two towns are linked by an intermediate station.
examples.cn: 两镇之间靠一个中间站相连。

examples.en: In this reaction an intermediate compound forms and quickly breaks up.
examples.cn: 在这个反应中会先生成一种中间化合物，随后很快分解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特米迪特」——网上找米迪特的秘诀，先从中级练起

root: 拉丁语 medius「中间的」→ inter-「在……之间」+ mediare「居于中间」→ intermediatus → 英语 intermediate。同族：medium、mediate、immediate、intermediary。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a middle level, a stage between two, products formed midway, and the people at that level.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：中间水平、介于两阶段之间、中途产物，以及处在该档的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp on the middle step between top and bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：上下台阶之间的那级台阶上放着灯。

branches.en: THE CLASS LIST: three columns with the middle filled first.
branches.cn: 班级分栏这条线：三栏中最先填满中间一栏。

branches.en: THE LARVA: a body holds a place between two forms.
branches.cn: 幼虫这条线：身体占据两种形态之间的位置。

branches.en: THE REACTION: halfway products appear and vanish.
branches.cn: 反应这条线：中途产物出现又消失。

branches.en: THE SWIMMER: a person occupies the middle band.
branches.cn: 游泳者这条线：人占据中档。

branches.en: THE LINK: bands of skill are stages on a path.
branches.cn: 连接线：技能档次就是路上的阶段。

intro.en: Intermediate = inter- "between" + medi- "middle" + -ate, an adjective ending.
intro.cn: intermediate = inter-「在……之间」+ medi-「中间」+ -ate（形容词词尾）。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius and mediare are recorded; intermediatus is medieval Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 medius 与 mediare 有记载，intermediatus 是中世纪拉丁语。

items.example: It places the middle between two ends.
items.exampleCN: 它把「中」安放在两端之间。

items.example: Also in medium and median.
items.exampleCN: 也见于 medium 与 median。

items.example: It supplies the participial stem.
items.exampleCN: 它提供分词词干。

items.example: It makes the word an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它使这个词成为形容词。

items.example: It forms intermediation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intermediation。

items.example: It forms intermediary.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intermediary。

items.example: It forms mediator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 mediator。

items.example: It denies the middle in immediate.
items.exampleCN: 它在 immediate 中否定「中间」。

latinEntries.meaning: to be in the middle, to mediate

definition_zh: 内部的；体内的；国内的；内心的
definition_en: existing or happening inside a person, object, organization, or country rather than outside it
core_image: 一层外壳包着的内腔，所有零件都在壳里面转动
scene: 修车师傅打开引擎盖，用手电照进机件之间的缝里。The internal parts of the engine need a full check.
sceneCN: 这里 internal 是「内部的」（第 1 个义项：位于物体里侧的），句意为引擎的内部零件需要全面检查。画面里的物件：引擎盖、手电、齿轮。

pos.zh: 形容词：内部的；体内的；国内的；内心的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在内部；内心里」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「内在性」
以 extern- 词根加 -al 构成的反义词，义为「外部的」
由同一词根构成，义为「扣押；做实习医生」

senses.title: Inside an object
senses.definition: located or happening inside a physical object rather than on its surface
senses.definitionCN: 位于某个实物内部，而不在其表面上
senses.example: A crack in the internal wall went unnoticed for years.
senses.exampleCN: 内墙里的一道裂缝多年无人发现。
senses.why: Latin internus meant "inward" and was built on the same in- as in, inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 internus 意为「向内的」，和 in、inside 共用同一个 in-。

senses.title: Inside the body
senses.definition: relating to the organs and processes hidden within a living body
senses.definitionCN: 与活体内部隐藏的器官及其运作有关的
senses.example: The doctor worried about internal bleeding after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔伤之后医生担心有内出血。
senses.why: Anatomy borrowed the spatial word: whatever lies beneath the skin is internal.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学借用了这个表示空间的词：皮肤底下的一切都叫 internal。

senses.title: Inside a country or group
senses.definition: belonging to the affairs of one country or organization, not involving outsiders
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个国家或组织自身事务、不涉及外部者的
senses.example: Internal trade rose while exports fell.
senses.exampleCN: 出口下降，国内贸易却增长了。
senses.why: Politics extended the shell metaphor to borders: things inside the border are internal.
senses.whyCN: 政治把这个「外壳」比喻扩展到国界：边界之内的事就是内部的。

senses.title: Inside the mind
senses.definition: existing in a person's private thoughts and feelings rather than being shown
senses.definitionCN: 存在于个人私下的想法与情感中而非表现出来的
senses.example: She fought an internal battle before answering the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 回那封信之前，她心里打了一场仗。
senses.why: The last step turns the word inward again, now to the mind rather than the body.
senses.whyCN: 最后一转又把词收回内部，只不过这回指心灵而非身体。

intro.en: Internal is a Latin adjective of location that English adopted whole in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: internal 是拉丁语中表示位置的形容词，十六世纪被英语整体吸收。

items.en: The preposition in meant "in, within".
items.cn: 介词 in 意为「在……之中」。

items.en: From it came the adjective internus, "situated within".
items.cn: 由它产生形容词 internus，义为「位于内部的」。

items.en: English took internus through French forms as internal in the sciences.
items.cn: 英语经由法语形式把 internus 引入，并在科学文献中写作 internal。

items.en: Anatomy and law used internal for organs and for home affairs.
items.cn: 解剖学与法律分别用 internal 指内脏与内政。

items.en: Modern psychology added the inward, private sense of the mind.
items.cn: 现代心理学又添上「内心、私密」这一层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the in- prefix; the near-meaning group holds words for what is hidden inside.
note.cn: 形近组共用 in- 前缀；近义组收表示「藏在里面」的词。

entries.definition: A trainee or, as a verb, to confine someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「实习生」，动词义为「扣押」。

entries.definition: The inside part of something, often of a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「内部」，常指房屋内部。

entries.definition: Very close and personal in relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「亲密的」，指关系亲近。

entries.definition: The nearer of two parts; the mental or secret side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的；内心的」，偏口语。

entries.definition: Of the home or of one's own country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「家里的；国内的」。

entries.definition: Kept out of sight on purpose or by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「隐藏的」，强调看不见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to things you already open up and look inside.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它挂在你已经会拆开往里看的东西上。

normal.en: in- in internal is the same in- as in inside.
normal.cn: internal 里的 in- 和 inside 里的 in- 是同一个。

normal.en: Add -al and a place becomes a quality: inside, therefore internal.
normal.cn: 加 -al 把位置变成性质：在里面，所以是内部的。

normal.en: Internal organs are the ones you cannot see.
normal.cn: internal organs 就是那些你看不见的器官。

normal.en: An internal email goes to staff only.
normal.cn: internal email 只发给本单位的人。

normal.en: Its mirror twin is external, with ex- for outside.
normal.cn: 它的镜像词是 external，用 ex- 表示外面。

abstract.en: Internal means the shell is doing the hiding.
abstract.cn: internal 的意思是那层壳在替你遮蔽。

abstract.en: A country's internal affairs are its own conversation.
abstract.cn: 一国的内部事务是它自己的对话。

abstract.en: The mind has an internal weather only its owner feels.
abstract.cn: 心灵有一片只有本人才感觉得到的内部天气。

examples.en: The company held an internal review of the failed launch.
examples.cn: 公司对那次失败的发布做了内部复盘。

examples.en: Internal doors should be wide enough for a wheelchair.
examples.cn: 室内的门应宽到能过轮椅。

examples.en: He kept his internal doubts away from the team.
examples.cn: 他把心里的疑虑藏着，没让团队看出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ tern + al——一切往「里」看都叫内部

root: 拉丁语 in「在内」→ internus「位于内部的」→ 英语 internal。反义为 external（ex-「在外」），同族有 intern、interior、internally。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: inside a thing, inside a body, inside a country or group, and inside a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：物体之内、身体之内、一国或团体之内，以及内心之中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything that stays behind the outer shell.
core.cn: 核心意象：留在外壳之内的一切。

branches.en: THE BOX: what lies within a physical object.
branches.cn: 盒子这条线：实物里侧的部分。

branches.en: THE BODY: organs kept under the skin.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：皮肤下面的器官。

branches.en: THE BORDER: affairs kept within one country.
branches.cn: 国界这条线：留在一国之内的政务。

branches.en: THE MIND: feelings never shown outside.
branches.cn: 心灵这条线：从未向外表露的情绪。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses hide something behind a surface.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都把东西藏在一个表面之后。

intro.en: Internal splits into the prefix in- "within", the stem intern-, and the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: internal 可拆为前缀 in-「在内」、词干 intern- 与形容词词尾 -al。

latinIntro.en: Latin in and internus are recorded; the deeper root is shared with inside.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in 与 internus 均有记载，更深层词根与 inside 同源。

items.example: The prefix marks the inside of a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出边界的内侧。

items.example: The stem carries the sense of location.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载位置意义。

items.example: It turns a place word into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 它把位置词变成性质词。

items.example: The adjective is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是直接来源。

items.example: The same stem names someone training inside a hospital.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干指在医院内部受训的人。

items.example: The comparative form of the same stem means the inner part.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干的比较级形式表示里侧。

items.example: It builds the opposite of in-.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 in- 的反义前缀。

items.example: The mirror word replaces in- with ex-.
items.exampleCN: 镜像词把 in- 换成了 ex-。

definition_zh: 实习；实习期；实习岗位
definition_en: a period of work in a company or organization, often for a student, in order to gain experience
core_image: 一张写着名字的工作牌，压在办公桌一角，旁边是还没拆封的笔记本
scene: 毕业生把新办的门禁卡挂在胸前，在办公室的空位上坐下开始整理资料。Her summer internship turned into a full job offer.
sceneCN: 这里 internship 是「实习」（第 1 个义项：为获取经验的短期工作），句意为她的暑期实习最后变成了正式录用。画面里的物件：门禁卡、办公桌、资料夹。

pos.zh: 名词：实习；实习期；实习岗位

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ship 构成，义为「实习生」
由 intern 加 -ing 构成，义为「实习的过程」
同一后缀构成，义为「学徒期」

senses.title: A first taste of work
senses.definition: a job taken mainly to learn, usually for a fixed period and often by a student
senses.definitionCN: 主要为学习而承担的工作，通常有固定期限，多为学生去做
senses.example: His first real internship was in a hospital kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他的第一份正经实习是在医院的厨房里。
senses.why: The suffix -ship means a state or role, so an internship is the condition of being an intern.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 表示状态或身份，所以 internship 就是「做 intern 的那段时光」。

senses.title: The period itself
senses.definition: the length of time during which someone works as an intern
senses.definitionCN: 某人做实习生所经历的那段时间
senses.example: The internship lasts twelve weeks with a review at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 这期实习持续十二周，结束时有一次评估。
senses.why: Time became as concrete as the job: the word names both the post and its run.
senses.whyCN: 时间变得和岗位一样具体：这个词同时指岗位和它的期限。

senses.title: A training step in a profession
senses.definition: a required supervised stage before full professional practice
senses.definitionCN: 正式执业之前必须经历的带督导训练阶段
senses.example: Medical internships keep young doctors under close watch.
senses.exampleCN: 医学实习让年轻医生处在密切看护之下。
senses.why: Law and medicine took the word over for the stage that makes someone fully qualified.
senses.whyCN: 法律与医学借用了这个词，指让人取得正式资格的那一段。

intro.en: Internship is an English coinage: the Latin-derived internal plus the native noun suffix -ship.
intro.cn: internship 是英语自造的：拉丁来源的 intern 加上本土名词后缀 -ship。

items.en: Internus "inner" described what lies within.
items.cn: internus「内部的」描述位于里侧的东西。

items.en: French interne named a doctor living inside a hospital.
items.cn: 法语 interne 指住在医院里的医生。

items.en: American English used intern for a graduate in training.
items.cn: 美式英语用 intern 指正在受训的毕业生。

items.en: -scipe was the native suffix for state or rank.
items.cn: 古英语的 -scipe 是表示状态或身份的本土后缀。

items.en: The two were joined in the early twentieth century as internship.
items.cn: 两者在二十世纪初合成 internship。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the intern stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for learning on the job.
note.cn: 形近组共用 intern 词干；近义组收其他表示「在工作中学习」的词。

entries.definition: Inside a thing, a body, or a country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的」。

entries.definition: The person doing such a period of work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「实习生」。

entries.definition: The state of being friends.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「友谊」，共用 -ship 后缀。

entries.definition: Training under a skilled master for years.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「学徒期」，跟师傅学多年。

entries.definition: A paid training post, often in Europe.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「带薪培训岗位」。

entries.definition: A trial period watched by an employer or court.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「试用期；缓刑」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to your own first days at a desk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它挂在你第一次坐进办公桌的那几天上。

normal.en: Intern plus -ship, the suffix of state, as in friendship.
normal.cn: intern 加 -ship，那个表示状态的后缀，如同 friendship。

normal.en: An intern is a person; an internship is the thing they go through.
normal.cn: intern 是人，internship 是他们经历的那件事。

normal.en: Summer internship is the phrase on every student's list.
normal.cn: summer internship 是每个学生清单上的词。

normal.en: The badge you wear is the sign of the internship.
normal.cn: 胸前那张工作牌就是实习的标志。

normal.en: -ship appears again in leadership and friendship.
normal.cn: -ship 还出现在 leadership 与 friendship 里。

abstract.en: An internship is a shadow before the real body arrives.
abstract.cn: 实习是真正上岗之前的一道影子。

abstract.en: It is a room you borrow so you can learn the trade.
abstract.cn: 那是你借用的房间，为的是学会这门手艺。

abstract.en: Practice, with a name tag.
abstract.cn: 练习，外加一张名牌。

examples.en: She found the internship through a friend of her mother.
examples.cn: 她通过母亲的一位朋友找到了这份实习。

examples.en: An internship at a newspaper taught him to write fast.
examples.cn: 在报社的实习教会他快速写稿。

examples.en: Unpaid internships became a topic of public debate.
examples.cn: 无薪实习成了公众讨论的话题。

dict_mnemonic.text: intern（实习生）+ ship（身份状态）——做实习生的那段身份

root: 拉丁语 internus「内部的」→ 法语 interne「驻院医生」→ 英语 intern，加本土后缀 -ship（状态、身份）成 internship。同族有 intern、internal、apprenticeship。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the learning post, the period it lasts, and the required stage in a profession.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：学习性质的岗位、这段岗位持续的时间，以及专业执业前的必修阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a borrowed desk where learning is the real salary.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张借来的桌子，真正的报酬是学到的本事。

branches.en: THE DESK: the first job taken to learn.
branches.cn: 书桌这条线：为学习而做的第一份工作。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR: the weeks the post lasts.
branches.cn: 日历这条线：这份岗位持续的周数。

branches.en: THE EXAM: the supervised stage before a licence.
branches.cn: 考试这条线：拿执照前的带督导阶段。

branches.en: THE LADDER: both senses sit on the way up to doing the job alone.
branches.cn: 阶梯线：两个义项都在通往独立执业的路上。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: training is measured out in fixed time.
branches.cn: 时钟线：训练总是按固定时长来计算。

intro.en: Internship pairs the Latin stem intern- "inside" with the Old English suffix -ship.
intro.cn: internship 把拉丁词干 intern-「在内」与古英语后缀 -ship 配在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin internus and French interne are recorded; -ship is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 internus 与法语 interne 均有记载，而 -ship 是日耳曼语本土后缀。

items.example: It names someone living inside an institution.
items.exampleCN: 它指住在机构内部的人。

items.example: The suffix also builds friendship.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也构成 friendship。

items.example: The noun is the base of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整条词的基础。

items.example: The adjective supplied the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干来自这个形容词。

items.example: The French form fixed the practical sense.
items.exampleCN: 法语形式定下了实用义。

items.example: It shows how -ship attaches to a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它示范了 -ship 如何接在名词后。

items.example: An apprenticeship is the older cousin.
items.exampleCN: apprenticeship 是它更年长的表亲。

items.example: The suffix works the same way here.
items.exampleCN: 后缀在这里起同样作用。

definition_zh: 人际的；人与人之间的；人际交往的
definition_en: existing or happening between people, or concerning the way people deal with one another
core_image: 两个人隔着一张小桌相对而坐，桌上没有文件，只有彼此的语气、眼神和说话之间的停顿
scene: 新主管上任第一周没有急着改流程，而是把每个人的名字、班次和最近家里的难处记进本子，开会前先问一句周末过得怎样。New managers are often advised to invest in interpersonal skills before they try to change any process.
sceneCN: 这里 interpersonal 指「与人打交道的能力」（第 2 个义项）；句意为：人们常建议新主管先投入人际技能，然后再去改动任何流程。

pos.zh: 人际的；人与人之间的；人际交往的

derivatives.zh: 在人际层面上（由 interpersonal 加副词后缀，把行为限定到人与人之间）
非个人的；没有人情味的（由否定前缀加 personal，把个人因素抽走）
非个人性；冷淡（由否定前缀加 personal 再加名词后缀，指抽掉个人情感后的状态）
个性化（由 personal 加表示过程的名词后缀，把公共的东西调整到某个人身上）

senses.title: Happening between people
senses.definition: existing or taking place between two or more people rather than inside one person
senses.definitionCN: 存在于或发生在两个或更多个人之间，而不是单个人内部
senses.example: The office layout changed the whole interpersonal atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室的布局改变了整个人际氛围。
senses.why: The prefix inter- means 'between', so the adjective marks whatever sits in the space that two people share rather than in either head alone.
senses.whyCN: 那个前缀意为「在……之间」，所以这个形容词标记的是两人共享的那片空间里的东西，而不是任何一个人脑中的东西。

senses.title: Skill in handling people
senses.definition: describing the ability to read, respect and manage other people in everyday dealings
senses.definitionCN: 描述在日常交往中读懂、尊重并处理好他人的能力
senses.example: Her interpersonal skills made a difficult client stay with the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的人际技巧让一个难缠的客户留在了公司。
senses.why: Once the space between people is recognised, it can be worked on like any other skill: listening, turn-taking and repair after a mistake.
senses.whyCN: 一旦承认两人之间那片空间存在，它就能像别的技能一样被练习：倾听、轮流说话、出错后修补。

senses.title: Friction between people
senses.definition: describing conflict, tension or misunderstanding that arises between people
senses.definitionCN: 描述人与人之间产生的冲突、紧张或误解
senses.example: The project failed not from bad planning but from interpersonal conflict.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目失败的原因不是计划糟糕，而是人际冲突。
senses.why: The same shared space can hold irritation as well as trust; the adjective simply locates the friction between the parties instead of inside one of them.
senses.whyCN: 同一片共享空间既能装信任，也能装恼火；这个形容词只是把摩擦定位在双方之间，而不是某一个人内部。

senses.title: Communication between people
senses.definition: describing the exchange of messages, meaning or feeling between people
senses.definitionCN: 描述人与人之间信息、意义或情感的交换
senses.example: Most of the misunderstanding came from interpersonal communication, not from the data.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分误解来自人际沟通，而不是数据本身。
senses.why: A message must be sent and received; when both ends are people, the channel between them is the thing the adjective describes.
senses.whyCN: 信息要被送出也要被接收；当两端都是人时，这个形容词描述的就是两人之间那条通道。

senses.title: Attraction and closeness
senses.definition: describing the pull of liking, trust or romantic interest that draws people together
senses.definitionCN: 描述把人们拉到一起的喜欢、信任或恋爱兴趣
senses.example: Interpersonal attraction grows when people find their views confirmed.
senses.exampleCN: 当人们发现对方印证了自己的观点时，人际吸引会增强。
senses.why: The line between two people has a direction and a strength; attraction is the force that shortens it, and the adjective names the field in which that force operates.
senses.whyCN: 两人之间那条线有方向也有强度；吸引就是缩短这条线的力，这个形容词命名的是这股力起作用的场域。

senses.title: Distance and personal space
senses.definition: describing how close people stand or sit in relation to one another and how that spacing is read
senses.definitionCN: 描述人们彼此站得多近、坐得多近，以及这种间距如何被解读
senses.example: Interpersonal distance shrinks when two people share a secret.
senses.exampleCN: 当两个人共享一个秘密时，人际距离会缩短。
